results.title: LTFRB opens over 8,000 TNVS slots for electric vehicles
results.description: The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has opened a total of 8,750 slots for ride-hailing service in Metro Manila and two other regions in Luzon. And this year’s approval of the opening slots is peculiar since it specifically gave special consideration for the electric vehicles as part of the measures for modern and environment-friendly public transportation. In Metro Manila for instance, all the 7,500 slots for Transport Network Vehicle Service (TNVS) are exclusive for electric vehicles, particularly Plug in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs) and Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs). Acting LTFRB Chairman Atty. Greg G. Pua, Jr. said special consideration was also provided for the 650 TNVS slots opened for Ilocos Region and 600 slots for Bicol Region as half of the approved slots are allocated for electric vehicles. In Ilocos Region, a total of 75 internal combustion engines and 75 non-internal combustion engines were allocated for Ilocos Norte for a total of 150. The same allocation and mode were approved for Ilocos Sur and La Union. For Pangasinan, the approved slots are 200—100 internal combustion engines and 100 non-internal combustion engines. In Bicol Region, half of the 600 TNVS slots approved are allocated for electric vehicles too. In the LTFRB memorandum circulars for the approval of the 8,750 slots, it emphasized that, “Conventional internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles, hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) other than PHEVs, and other vehicle technologies that do not fall within the BEV or PHEV classifications shall not be eligible for the slots opened herein. “The classification of the vehicle as a BEV or PHEV shall be based on its registration and classification by the Land Transportation Office (LTO) and other applicable government standards and issuances,” the circulars added. Pua explained that the move is in line with the direction of the national government for a modern and environment-friendly public transportation. In his recent State of the Nation Address, President Marcos committed support to modern public transportation and said the goal is to have half of all the vehicles in the road to be electric vehicles by 2040. Pua said all the decision on the opening of the slots was based on the result of the monitoring and study about the prevailing transport conditions which indicates insufficient TNVS allocation to serve the geographic coverage and increasing volume of commuters in. Metro Manila, Ilocos Region and Bicol Region. He said the feedback from various stakeholders also boosted the need to increase the allocation due to prevailing passenger demand. A separate review and study pointed to increased economic activities as one of the major factors—expanding urban, commercial, government, and tourism centers that generate increasing demand for safe, reliable, accessible, and technology-enabled transport services for residents and visitors. According to the LTFRB, the application for the available slots will start once the memorandum circulars relating to this decision is published in a newspaper with general circulation
